The intended client of IskoMatic is the Local Youth Development Office (LYDO) of the Municipality of Santa Cruz, Laguna. The office is the target organization for the scholarship applicant screening and management workflow. The system is designed for authorized LYDO personnel who receive applicant information, maintain scholarship records, review screening results, schedule interviews, and record official scholarship decisions.

Applicants are treated as walk-in submitters. They provide their information and supporting requirements to office personnel, who encode and manage the records through the desktop application. The current implementation includes staff account registration, sign-in, account approval, and role-based access. The software distinguishes ADMIN and LYDO_OFFICIAL roles.

Scholarship application processing involves collecting and reviewing personal, academic, household, financial, and eligibility information. When records are maintained manually or across separate files, retrieving applicant information, tracking application progress, organizing interviews, and reviewing applicants consistently can require repetitive work and make record monitoring difficult.

Problem statement: The LYDO scholarship workflow needs a centralized system for managing applicant and application records, supporting consistent initial eligibility screening, organizing interviews, and recording official scholarship decisions while keeping final selection authority with authorized office personnel.

CHAPTER II: SYSTEM ANALYSIS AND DESIGN

IskoMatic is a desktop-based application that centralizes scholarship applicant records and supports the staff workflow from application encoding through initial screening, interview management, and official decision recording. The AI screening result is advisory; authorized LYDO personnel remain responsible for reviewing applications and making final decisions.
Registers staff requests, authenticates approved accounts, and applies staff roles.
Restricts system use to approved personnel and supports accountability.
Maintains applicant profiles and scholarship-specific application details.
Centralizes records and makes information easier to retrieve and update.
Applies eligibility rules and runs a saved Random Forest model for eligible records.
Helps staff prioritize review without replacing official judgment.
Schedules interviews, records outcomes, and stores official decisions and reasons.
Organizes later workflow stages and preserves decision history.

Architecture explanation: The desktop interface is built with Tauri and React/TypeScript. It communicates with a local Python backend bridge over HTTP. The backend validates inputs, applies workflow and eligibility rules, accesses the MySQL database, and invokes the saved scikit-learn Random Forest model for screening. The database stores applicant, application, screening, interview, decision, model-version, and audit records. The current source also creates staff account and session tables at runtime. The
desktop UI uses the local bridge at 127.0.0.1:8765; the Vite development server address is for development and is not a public hosted service

Context diagram / Level 0: The applicant submits the application form and supporting requirements to LYDO personnel. The authorized staff member encodes and manages the information through IskoMatic. The system returns application status and screening information to staff, who use the results during review, interview scheduling, and official decision recording.

Level 1 DFD: The workflow is divided into applicant and application management, applicant screening, interview management, scholarship decision management, and report/output functions. The data stores shown in the design include applicant/application records, screening results, interview records, and scholarship decisions.

DFD explanation: Applicant information and application details enter through staff encoding. The screening process reads application data, checks the configured eligibility rules, and stores model output in screening results. Interview records are linked to applications, and authorized staff record the official scholarship decision. The source implementation additionally supports staff authentication and session data.

The applicant is an external participant who submits information and requirements in person. The software users are LYDO staff accounts. The current implementation distinguishes ADMIN and LYDO_OFFICIAL roles. ADMIN can review staff registration requests and manage account access. Authorized staff can manage applicants and applications, run screening, schedule interviews, and view workflow information. Decision operations are subject to backend authorization checks.

The updated conceptual class diagram is derived from the implemented database entities. Applicant stores personal and contact information. Application stores scholarship-specific information and is linked to one applicant. ScreeningResult stores a prediction and references the model version used. Interview stores appointment and interview outcome details. ScholarshipDecision stores the official decision and reason. ModelVersion stores model metadata and evaluation metrics. CHAPTER IV: SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS AND FUTURE DEVELOPMENT
Applicant record handling: the repository includes applicant creation, retrieval, update, search, and archive operations. Archiving preserves records instead of permanently deleting them.
Application workflow: application records are linked to applicants, and service-level rules restrict which status transitions are permitted.
Screening support: the supplied source includes a saved Random Forest model, eligibility checks, screening explanations, ranking logic, and persistence of screening results with model information.
Human decision control: the decision service defines which official decisions are available based on application stage and interview completion. The model remains a decision-support tool.
Complete and verify database backup and restore, including file integrity checks and a documented recovery procedure, to reduce the risk of data loss.

Add PDF and Excel report generation if required by LYDO; the supplied source documentation currently identifies applicant CSV export, so other report formats should not be described as implemented without verification
Provide controlled model retraining, model evaluation, version selection, and rollback, with saved training parameters and reproducible evaluation records.
Expand audit-log review features, including search, filtering, and export, and verify that audit records are protected against unauthorized changes.
Conduct complete usability, security, performance, and user-acceptance testing in the intended Windows and MySQL environment.
Review eligibility thresholds and screening rules with authorized LYDO personnel before using the system with real scholarship applicants.
Evaluate future model versions using authorized, representative, privacy-protected data, including analysis of false positives, false negatives, and possible differences in error rates.
Prepare and verify a reliable installation and maintenance procedure for transferring the desktop system to the LYDO workstation.

Deployment consideration: applicant records may contain personal, academic, household, and financial information. The office should protect the workstation, database credentials, database service, backup files, and exported records through appropriate access controls and secure operating procedures.
